correctness.rationale: Two-state stochastic transition maps are affine contractions on [0,1]; any nontrivial unique maximum forces all suffix slopes nonzero and letter maps nonidentity. Swapping adjacent unequal letters changes final acceptance by the signed suffix-product times (1−s_a)(1−s_b)(h_b−h_a). All forced inequalities must embed in a strict fixed-point order, hence the graph must be acyclic. The six inequalities for 0120102 contradict one another for all slope signings. The source verify.py enumerates every 3-symbol-surjective word of length 3..7, every sign pattern and every order; an independent Kahn-topological-sort implementation confirms the exact table (6,36,150,540,1806) with 48 failures at n=7 and 8 canonical classes. Prefixed suffixes retain the inequalities; the cited published three-state construction supplies exact equality, not just a lower bound. The proof is necessary-only for two states; it does not prove the first genuinely ternary word of complexity 3 has length seven.

value.rationale: This is a nontrivial structural necessary obstruction on a natural multi-letter generalization of probabilistic automatic complexity. It gives the first complete sharp small-length failure census for that obstruction and infinite positive-density families of exact maximal three-state complexity; this is neither a renamed binary classification nor a bare length-seven lookup.

final_claim: A two-state PFA uniquely maximizing a nonconstant word requires an acyclic signed adjacent-swap graph for some letter-slope signing. Exactly 48 surjective ternary length-seven words fail this necessary test, in eight relabeling classes; no lengths 3–6 fail. Each forbidden seven-letter suffix forces exact PFA complexity 3 over larger alphabets, yielding at least 48*binom(q,3)*q^(n−7) words of complexity 3.
